subject: Order form: invoicing cadence, proration, and tax responsibility
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@sunwavehealth.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: payables@sunwavehealth.com
Date: 2025-10-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Order form questions — invoicing cadence & tax

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team is excited to move forward. We received the draft order form and have a couple of operational questions before our procurement/finance team will sign: 

1) Invoicing cadence: the order form shows a single upfront invoice for the committed amount, then monthly usage invoices. Can you confirm whether SunWave can request a quarterly invoice schedule (one invoice per quarter) instead? Our AP system prefers quarterly billing for SaaS line items.

2) Proration on activation: we expect a staged rollout across three business units. Will the activation/credit proration be applied at invoice time automatically, or do we need an invoice-level line item explanation?

3) Tax responsibility: due to our EU subsidiary, we need clarity on VAT handling for prepay vs usage. If Redwood issues invoices from the US entity, do you have a certificate or process for reverse charge evidence?

Attached is our PO stub (SunWave_PO_88971.pdf) — procurement will need a formal invoice path before issuing the PO.

Can you loop in finance/legal? If we can get a short runbook for AP (how invoices will land, remit entity, and tax evidence), procurement can proceed.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Senior Procurement Manager | SunWave Health
elena.morales@sunwavehealth.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@sunwavehealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-10-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoicing cadence & tax

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear note and the PO stub. Looping in Kimberly (finance) and Ben (sales) so we can give concrete answers and a short AP runbook. 

Short answers up front:
- Quarterly invoice cadence: we can support quarterly invoicing for committed amounts (prepay) as a billing schedule exception — need to confirm for usage-billed items (those typically remain monthly).
- Proration: activation proration will be reflected as line items on the invoice; we can include an invoice summary sheet for your AP team showing per-entity credits/activation dates.
- Tax/VAT: Redwood issues invoices from our US entity by default; for EU reverse-charge we will accept a VAT ID and include the reverse-charge notation. Kimberly will confirm the exact evidence required.

Next steps: Ben, can you confirm whether SunWave prefers the committed prepay to be invoiced quarterly or billed upfront and then refunded/credited quarterly? Also attaching a redline of the order form (Redline_OrderForm_v3.docx) that clarifies the invoicing language we propose.

Elena — if you can share the legal billing contact and the VAT ID for the EU subsidiary we’ll include that in the runbook. I’ve also attached an activation schedule template (Activation_Schedule.xlsx) that your rollout team can fill out to drive proration line items.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.ai

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@sunwavehealth.com>, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-10-12T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoicing cadence & tax

Elena — quick clarifications from the commercial side. Appreciate the PO stub, that moves things fast.

1) Committed prepay options we can support:
   • Upfront annual prepay (single invoice)
   • Quarterly prepay (4 invoices, one per quarter) — this is a billing schedule exception we can set in the order form (no price change)
   • Monthly prepay (if you prefer smaller tranches)

2) Usage overages: those are still invoiced monthly by default. If you want quarterly consolidated usage invoices we can bundle usage lines, but that will add ~5 business days to settlement while we aggregate the month-by-month tallies.

3) Proration / activation credits: we will populate invoice line items that reconcile activation credits to the committed amount. If you provide the Activation_Schedule.xlsx back with dates by entity, finance can generate an invoice summary appendix.

4) Tax: Kimberly will confirm the reverse-charge and evidence flow, but typically we accept your EU VAT ID and mark the invoice accordingly. If SunWave requires Redwood to invoice an EU entity instead of the US entity we’ll need to involve legal for entity-level invoicing (this affects currency and contract entity).

If this approach works I’ll update the order form language in the attached redline and we can get procurement to issue PO + sign.

Best,
Ben Carter
Head of Commercials | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@sunwavehealth.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-10-13T14:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoicing cadence & tax

Hi Elena — Kimberly from Finance here. Thanks for the PO stub. A few operational details and the evidence we’ll need to satisfy both US and EU bookkeeping: 

1) Preferred flow for SunWave (recommended):
   - Commit prepay invoiced quarterly (we’ll issue one invoice per quarter for the committed tranche).
   - Monthly usage billed and remitted monthly; if you prefer aggregated quarterly usage invoices, note that payment terms will be NET45 instead of NET30 to allow for aggregation and reconciliation.

2) Proration and activation credits:
   - Provide Activation_Schedule.xlsx with date and entity fields filled. We will attach an "Invoice Appendix" that lists activation credits applied per invoice line so your AP has clear matching fields (invoice reference, activation date, entity code).

3) Tax / VAT handling:
   - For EU reverse-charge, please supply the EU subsidiary VAT ID and a contact who can sign the reverse-charge certificate. We will include the VAT ID and the reverse-charge note on the invoice.
   - If SunWave requires Redwood to invoice from an EU legal entity, we need a contract amendment (MSA entity swap) — that triggers legal review and local invoicing terms (currency, VAT registration).

4) PO & remittance details:
   - We can accept the PO you attached; please confirm the remit entity and the billing email (payables@sunwavehealth.com is fine).

Attachments: we will upload a clean invoice template and the redlined order form to the HubSpot deal and send a DocuSign after you confirm the quarterly prepay option.

Action items:
   • Elena — confirm quarterly prepay vs upfront (one-time) for committed tranche and provide EU VAT ID if applicable.
   • Jasmine / Ben — update order form language to reflect the quarterly prepay option and the invoice appendix requirement.

Kimberly Park
Senior Accounting Manager | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
